name: Lifecycle and updates
notes: Install, login, quit, single instance, data folder, updates

features.feature: The DMG installs on a fresh Mac; first run chooses the data folder (or the default) and downloads a speech model (now or later; an interrupted download fails cleanly; the model in use can't be removed)
Echo starts at login when set to, and doesn't when not; an installed app's first run turns it on (a dev build's doesn't)
Quit saves the window's notes first, ends every process, and Echo starts normally again (`echoctl app start`)
Only one Echo runs at a time
Changing the data folder restarts Echo on the new one and leaves the old one alone
Notifications come from Echo and open its window; "Update available" asks to install
An update is offered, installs after saving and quitting, keeps everything, and never while a call records; on the newest version nothing is offered
Closing the window keeps Echo in the menu bar and the Dock (unless Hide from the Dock); a Dock click opens it again

An Echo macOS runs translocated (a quarantined app not moved by Finder) never records its temporary path: app-path, the echoctl link and the login item point at the copy in Applications, or Echo asks to be moved there

After an update, the window shows What's new once: the items of every version since the last one seen, newest first under version headers, each an icon, a title of a few words and one plain sentence; a reopen doesn't show it again; a fresh install (no calls yet) shows nothing
What's new closes with ×, Esc or Got it, and an item's Show me closes it and opens that item's place in Echo

What's new is reachable again from ⌘K ("What's new"), Settings → General, beside Echo's version, and the tray menu ("What's new…": a closed window opens on Today with it, an open one shows it over its view): every version's items, newest first
